title: When deleting an approval allowlist, restate every surviving guard at the deletion site
statement: If a consent gate is deliberately removed (e.g. 'autonomous mode IS the standing consent'), write the decision as a historical note at the removal site that enumerates each remaining bound by name and states plainly which previously-held-back actions now fire unattended — so the risk was accepted explicitly, not discovered later.

title: Isolate concurrent sessions in worktrees and log intent in a ledger
statement: When several agent or CLI sessions edit one checkout: never stash, because it sweeps other sessions' in-flight and untracked work into a place nobody looks; give any scope larger than one file its own worktree; commit atomically rather than accumulating hours of uncommitted work; and stage per path, verifying the staged set before committing, because the index may already hold another session's files. Physical isolation and a shared intent ledger are complementary, not alternatives.

title: End every decision record with what this increment must not touch
statement: Small numbered decision records keep structural change reviewable, but the reusable half is the closing fence: an explicit out-of-scope list naming the files and behaviours the change must not affect. It is what keeps an agent-driven or unfamiliar increment narrow, and it turns the review question from a matter of taste into something checkable against the diff.

title: Prototype visual variants against one shared data-and-actions hook
statement: When several directions for the same surface are explored in parallel, extract the fetch, derivation and mutation handlers into one hook first. Each variant then owns only filters and layout, the comparison stays honest because behaviour is identical across them, and consolidating the winner becomes a deletion rather than a rewrite. The view model outlives the throwaway fixtures that first shaped it.

title: Ship a derived-data pipeline gated off by default and best-effort
statement: When adding a pipeline that derives rows from existing writes, gate the whole thing on an environment flag defaulting to off, have every promoter log and swallow its own errors, and make re-promotion an idempotent no-op. Production behaviour is then unchanged through the bake-in window and the parent write can never fail because of the new feature. Keep created, already-existed and failed as three distinct outcomes.

title: Don't let module docs promise auto-reconnect and retries that don't exist
statement: The `connection.rs` header advertises 'auto-reconnect' but no reconnect path exists: `max_retries` is initialized to 3 and `#[allow(dead_code)]`, `retry_count` is written 0 and never incremented, and health-check failure disconnects and gives up. Docs describing unimplemented behavior mislead every future reader.

title: A 'single source of truth' comment without landed consumers is a lie the next reader trusts
statement: Declaring a shared primitive the SSOT ("the two named components are thin wrappers") while both consumers still exist as full independent implementations leaves three near-identical config maps drifting, conflicting exported types with the same name, and one copy hardcoding English while the others translate. A consolidation PR must delete or actually re-implement the wrappers — or not write the comment.

title: Operator-facing paste-out artifacts stay deliberately locale-independent English
statement: Generated artifacts whose destination is outside the app — run reports pasted into ledgers, PRs, and handoff notes — are deliberately exempt from the i18n system: they render in stable English technical register via a pure, locale-independent builder. The exemption is scoped by destination (artifact leaves the app) and stated in the module doc so it survives the repo's otherwise-mandatory no-hardcoded-English rule.

title: Unchecked mirrors of the real gates — a second CI pipeline, contributor docs — rot into contradicting them
statement: Any hand-maintained mirror of an enforced pipeline (a parallel CI config for another forge, a CONTRIBUTING guide restating the checks) decays silently: fixes land in the primary and never propagate, until the mirror actively teaches the pre-fix behavior. Either machine-check the mirror against the primary, or delete it and link to the one source of truth.

title: Say what breaks if each tuning constant is halved or doubled
statement: A magic number with no justification is deleted or 'simplified' by the next reader. Collect them into one named block per module and justify each as the consequence of moving it in either direction, so the constant defends itself against a well-meaning edit. Where two constants must satisfy an invariant, assert it at load rather than trusting a future change to remember the pairing.

title: Label deliberately dormant code with its revival checklist
statement: Code that is intentionally ahead of its consumer, or parked pending a decision, reads exactly like abandoned code six months later. State in the module header why it exists, what it deliberately does not do yet, which stage will consume it, and the concrete steps to revive it — and attach that note to the dead-code suppression or the disabled feature flag, so the suppression explains itself rather than needing archaeology.

title: Comment the measurement that killed the previous design
statement: The most useful comment in a codebase is not what the code does but the measurement, incident or rejected alternative that makes its current shape non-negotiable. Write the number, the date and the observed symptom into the module that fixes it. Without it the next reader sees an arbitrary constraint and removes it; with it, the constraint defends itself — and it is worth correcting a comment that has since been proven wrong.

title: Give a sprawling feature folder an owns / does NOT own table
statement: When one feature grows into many sibling modules, a co-located map naming per module both what it owns and what it explicitly does not is what actually stops duplication — the positive column alone is just a directory listing. Add the rule for where cross-module helpers go, record the intentional exceptions to the naming convention, and require the new row in the same change that creates the folder.

title: Back a decision-matrix README with a compile-time inventory assertion
statement: Where several modules share vocabulary and get mistaken for each other, prose does not help: write the README as a matrix of input, output artifact, caller and which one to extend, followed by the anti-patterns already seen in practice. Then back it with a registry constant and a compile-time length assertion, so adding a variant fails the build until both the registry and the README row move in the same change.

title: Route all codegen through one runner wired into the build's own pre-hooks
statement: Every generated artifact (seeds, checksums, locale splits, binding regen, environment self-healing) should be invoked from a single runner script attached to the package manager's pre-hooks (predev/prebuild, pre<task>), so 'run the app' is the only ritual. A second registration point — a bundler buildStart plugin, an ad-hoc npm script — both duplicates cost and silently diverges when a new task is added to only one list.

title: Grade lint boundaries by maturity: hard error at the mandatory seam, warn plus a dated inventory of known violations at aspirational seams
statement: Not every architectural boundary can be an error on day one. Enforce the non-negotiable seam at error severity; for boundaries with known legacy violations, set the rule to warn AND record in the config itself which files violate it, as of when, and where they should migrate — so the warning stays a tracked debt instead of ambient noise, and can be promoted to error when the inventory empties.

title: Machine-check the source-to-docs coupling, with a real dismissal path
statement: Keep the map from source paths to their coupled surfaces as data, and run it at the end of each session to nag when feature code changed and its documentation, tour or marketing counterpart did not. Filter mechanical churn before matching, make each surface satisfiable by editing anything under its root so the gate is cheap to clear, and pair the nag with a legitimate one-sentence dismissal — a gate with no escape is a gate everyone learns to disable.

title: Tier git hooks by cost, and never let one rewrite the tree
statement: Split local gates by what they cost: the commit hook runs on staged files only and must stay within a few seconds, while type-checking and full suites move to the push hook, each glob-scoped so an unrelated commit pays nothing. And make it a hard rule that hooks never stash, restore or rewrite the working tree — with concurrent sessions sharing one checkout, a tree-mutating hook clobbers work nobody will think to look for. Optional tooling should skip with a hint rather than block.

title: Turn every repeated review comment into a local lint rule
statement: Conventions a reviewer keeps restating — raw utility classes that have token equivalents, hand-rolled modal backdrops, direct clipboard calls, whole-store subscriptions — belong in the linter, not the checklist. Ship a rule at warning level while its migration is in flight and at error level once the invariant is absolute, so the severity itself documents which conventions are negotiable and which are not.

title: Audit a curated collection's members against live canon status, and suggest — never auto-apply — replacements
statement: A curated collection (playbook, checklist, template) is a promise that following it applies current doctrine, so a member whose source item was deprecated, rejected, or deleted is worse than a missing one — it actively teaches something the organization abandoned. Compute staleness as a pure derived view (only 'adopted' counts as live), resolve a likely replacement through explicit relationship edges with a precedence (supersedes beats governs-parent), and surface both to the curator: which phase a replacement belongs in is judgement the system cannot make.

title: Advance a pinned dependency floor only with a dossier of fixes that land on your exact call surface
statement: Keep the minimum-version floor of a critical dependency (here: the Claude CLI) as an annotated in-code dossier: each floor advance cites the specific upstream releases whose fixes land on YOUR call surface (headless -p, stream-json, stdin-pipe spawn on Windows), explicitly dismisses release notes for surfaces you never reach, and dates each entry to the research run that produced it. The floor becomes an auditable decision log instead of a magic number.

title: Document a latent hazard at its site with the exact condition that makes it real, instead of fixing it speculatively
statement: When an audit finds a registration keyed in a way that WOULD be a bug under a call pattern that doesn't exist yet (re-entry for the same session id stealing the first attempt's cancel flag), and the proper fix is a real design change, leave the shape as-is with a comment that names the sibling bug it mirrors, states why the current key is load-bearing, and spells out the precise future condition under which the fix becomes mandatory.

title: Grade maturity against an explicit rubric with archetype-scaled targets, not one absolute bar
statement: Replace magic numbers buried in score weights with a rubric-as-data: each dimension declares a weight, a pure accessor for current attainment (0..1 position on that dimension's ladder), and a per-archetype TARGET (solo < team < org). The score is the weighted % of targets met given the subject's own archetype — so a solo prototype isn't held to an org-grade bar, and the bar itself is reviewable and tunable in one table instead of scattered through the scoring code.

title: Rank remediation by impact-per-effort — score lift ÷ action cost tier — and drop gaps with no executable action
statement: Turn a diagnostic scorecard into a work queue by scoring every below-target gap as the composite-% it would unlock (dimension weight × remaining gap ÷ total weight) divided by an effort tier for the fixing lever (config toggle < automated scan < wiring a connector < an agent task). Map each dimension to its lever in one table; a gap whose lever has no currently-applicable action is dropped rather than shown as an inert row. The ranked list answers 'what's the single best thing to do next, across everything?'.
